data.title: Profitability Isn’t Absolute Criterion for Judging Robotic Firms, Unitree Founder Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 27 -- Profitability is not an absolute criterion for judging robotic companies, as they are mostly still in the red because they are exploring modern technological development, according to the founder of Chinese robotics giant Unitree Robotics.

Profitability is important, but it is not the only way to measure companies’ development, Wang Xingxing, who is also Unitree’s chairman and chief executive officer, said at the WISE Business Conference in Beijing yesterday. “If there are good technological directions, such as artificial intelligence, we will definitely increase investment, which may lead to a decline in profitability.”

Unitree is one of the few robotics companies in the black despite its heavy research and development investment. It reported a net profit of CNY387 million (USD58.1 million) in the third quarter, while its R&D spending surged 191 percent to CNY263 million from a year earlier due to increased investment in embodied AI and computing power.

The implementation of robots does not need to wait until AI is fully mature, Wang noted. Even with the arrival of the artificial general intelligence era, the widespread use of robots will still require an industrial ramp-up, which may take a long time.

As the industry enters mass production, China’s robot output will likely surpass automobile output within five to 10 years, Wang predicted.

Last year, China’s output of robots in a broad sense and cars was 19.35 million units and 34.78 million units, respectively, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics. However, only about 773,000 industrial robots were made last year.

The Chinese output of humanoid robots was even lower, exceeding 40,000 units in the first half of this year, according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The figure is expected to surpass 100,000 units this year.

AGI models are generally beneficial for the embodied AI industry, Wang said. “The progress of general large language models or multimodal large models in recent months has made the world more confident that there will be breakthroughs in AI models for the robotics field in the next few years, or even just one or two years.”

Recent years of practice have fully proven that AI models or models trained on more data work better when applied to robotics, Wang explained. After incorporating robot data into an LLM, the model’s reasoning, decision-making ability, and understanding of the physical world improve.

Unitree is promoting cooperation with foreign LLM companies, expecting to produce a brain-cerebellum integrated system by the end of this year or next year, Wang unveiled.

However, LLMs have not yet solved the problems that arise when robots interact with the physical world. In scenarios of fine operation, the success rate of robots still needs to be improved, he added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Alibaba Slashes Stake in Chinese Courier ZTO Express for Second Time This Year
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 27 -- Alibaba Group Holding has cut its stake in Chinese courier ZTO Express for the second time this year, cashing out almost USD1 billion in total, with the e-commerce giant continuing to boost artificial intelligence spending while scaling back external investments.

Three Alibaba subsidiaries sold 25 million class A ordinary shares of ZTO Express at USD19.28 per American depositary receipt for USD482 million on Nov. 24, the Hangzhou-based firm said in a filing to the US Securities and Exchange Commission the next day. Its stake in the carrier dropped to 2.9 percent, or about 21.94 million shares.

In 2018, a consortium led by Alibaba and its logistics arm Cainiao Smart Logistics Network invested USD1.4 billion for about 10 percent of ZTO Express, planning to deepen ties in pickup and delivery, warehousing, cross-border logistics, and smart logistics. On Sept. 21 this year, two Alibaba units sold 25 million ZTO Express shares at USD20 each in a USD500 million deal, reducing the stake to 6.1 percent.

Under the initial agreement, the investors subscribed at USD17.28 per share, meaning that this year's two sales were priced about 15.9 percent and 11.6 percent above the purchase price.

Alibaba previously held equity in all four major Chinese express delivery companies, acquiring a stake in YTO Express in 2015 and in STO Express and Yunda Holdings in 2019.

However, Alibaba slashed its stake in YTO Express to 14.8 percent from 20.8 percent in three transactions between April last year and this July worth more than CNY3 billion. In addition, according to Yunda's third-quarter earnings report last year, Alibaba was no longer among its top ten shareholders.

However, Alibaba's stake in STO Express has remained stable. As of the end of last quarter, Cainiao Supply Chain still held a 25 percent stake in the courier, unchanged from the end of last year, making it its largest single shareholder.

Taobao, an e‑commerce platform under Alibaba, also sold its entire holding of just over 45.8 million shares in SF Intra-city in September, according to disclosures of interests filed with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

While trimming external investments, Alibaba is increasing its AI spending. According to its financial report for the fiscal second quarter released on Nov. 19, capital expenditure surged 60 percent to CNY50.5 billion (USD7.7 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from a year earlier, mainly due to accelerating expansion of computing capacity, rising prices of various chip components, higher central processing unit demand from customers' continued adoption of AI agents, and fluctuations in procurement cycles.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: German Businesses Deepen Involvement in China’s Innovation Ecosystem
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- Executives at a China-Germany business conference have hailed the progress in industrial cooperation between the two countries.

The relationship used to be primarily a blend of German design and Chinese labor, but now it features closer integration of research and development, deeper technical collaboration, and long-term partnerships with local clients, said representatives at the fourth AHK Greater China Xceleration Days, which is being held in Shanghai.

China is one of the fastest markets for innovation, with an extremely short cycle from research and development, testing, and implementation to market launch, said Martin Hofmann, chairman of the board of directors for North China and Northeast China of the German Chamber of Commerce in China. 

German enterprises are deeply impressed by the so-called “China speed," Hofmann added, and are eager to engage deeply with China’s innovation ecosystem and bring the insights gained back to Germany.

“The pace of the consumer electronics industry is faster than that of semiconductors and automobiles, which is why we established an innovation experience center here in China that is closer to our customers,” Hu Xiaolong, head of product development for Henkel Adhesive Technologies’ electronics division in China, told Yicai during the event.

The company’s Inspiration Center Shanghai, which opened in September last year, is its second-largest globally, after the one in Dusseldorf, Germany, where the firm is headquartered.

German injection molding giant KraussMaffei has also moved beyond simple equipment sales, and is deepening its collaboration with a Shanghai-based manufacturer of reusable logistics containers. 

In response to complex challenges related to adjusting material formulations and process optimization during the recycling and reuse of these containers -- covering the entire lifecycle from material recovery and manufacturing to end-use -- the partnership has resolved critical pain points for Chinese clients around full-chain digital logistics management, KraussMaffei said, adding that it also offers a replicable model for green manufacturing on a global scale.

China’s booming robotics sector has likewise captured the interest of German firms. Bavaria-based FMC³ Robotics focuses on embodied intelligent brain solutions and set up its first office in China in Jiaxing, Zhejiang province a year ago. Jiang Nan, chief marketing officer, told Yicai the rise of new energy vehicles and intelligent driving in China has had a huge impact on German companies. 

FMC³ Robotics is now working closely with Chinese partners to deploy robots equipped with its “embodied intelligent brain” in European production lines, Jiang said, to connect Germany’s industrial environment with Chinese technologies.

Robotics is a key area that companies need to explore with their Chinese partners, said Ni Kefan, technical head of Henkel Adhesive Technologies’ electronics division for the Asia Pacific region. The solutions required are "not entirely brand new," he said, as technologies previously developed for consumer electronics such as mobile phones can be adapted for this field.

For example, robots rely on numerous sensors for environmental perception, a function with parallels to components such as mobile phone camera modules. Also, the high-speed operation of robot joints generates heat, requiring thermal interface materials to conduct and dissipate that heat, an area that aligns perfectly with Henkel’s existing product portfolio.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: Chinese Research Team Unveils Brain-Computer Interface Device for Hard-to-Treat Depression
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- DeepAxtiv, an invasive brain-computer interface system designed to deliver precision treatment for patients with treatment-resistant depression, has been launched by a research team led by Zhejiang University’s College of Computer Science and Technology and its Frontier Science Center for Brain Science and Brain-Machine Integration in collaboration with several partner institutions.

Treatment-resistant depression accounts for about 30 percent of all depression cases, a senior expert in neuroscience told Yicai. Patients are generally classified as having treatment-resistant depression if they fail to respond adequately to at least two antidepressant medications administered at appropriate doses and for an adequate duration,

Existing treatment options for the condition all have certain limitations, the expert said. For example, deep brain stimulation, which involves surgically implanting electrodes into the brain to deliver electrical stimulation, has shown limited efficacy. This is partly because brain activity patterns and responses to stimulation vary considerably from one patient to another, making it difficult to apply a standardized treatment protocol across patients.

Studies have found that deep brain stimulation has an average response rate of around 54 percent and a symptom remission rate of about 41 percent, the expert said, citing clinical data. Patients typically take one to two years to respond to treatment.

By contrast, the DeepAxtiv system has a 100 percent response rate and a symptom remission rate of 83 percent, the development team said, citing the results of prospective clinical trials conducted on six patients with treatment-resistant depression. Treatment effects emerged within one to eight weeks after the therapy began, the team said.

The system’s key advantage lies in its ability to personalize deep brain stimulation by selecting treatment parameters tailored to each patient’s individual condition, Zhang Hongjian, assistant to the dean of the Oriental Pan-Vascular Devices Innovation College at University of Shanghai for Science and Technology, told Yicai.

Clinical Breakthroughs

“The DeepAxtiv system utilizes three core technologies to provide individualized, closed-loop neural regulation for treatment-resistant depression,” Yang Yuxiao, a researcher at Zhejiang University’s Frontier Science Center for Brain Science and Brain-Machine Integration and a member of the DeepActiv research team, told Yicai.

The three technologies are iTarget, which identifies the optimal treatment target for each patient, iSense, which translates brain activity into quantifiable neurophysiological indicators to monitor depressive symptoms, and iAdapt, which precisely optimizes stimulation parameters through adaptive adjustments.

The biggest advantage of DeepAxtiv is that it takes effect rapidly, said Sun Rong, consulting director at US business consultancy firm Frost & Sullivan's China branch. Conventional deep-brain stimulation devices often take one to two years to produce noticeable results, during which time patients may have a high risk of suicide.

“The development team plans to begin registration clinical trials next year,” Hu Xiongjie, general manager of Hangzhou Qingshi Yongjun Medical Equipment, one of the companies involved in launching the DeepAxtiv system, told Yicai.

"The team aims to obtain what it hopes will be the world’s first medical device registration approval for a brain-computer interface system designed for precision treatment of treatment-resistant depression, potentially providing an approved clinical treatment option for nearly 100 million patients worldwide including close to 30 million in China,” he added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Kim Taylor

data.title: CAAM to Scrutinize Supplier Payment Practices at Major Chinese Carmakers
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 17 -- The China Association of Automobile Manufacturers will evaluate supplier payment practices at 17 major domestic carmakers, including BYD and SAIC Motor, at the request of regulators seeking to standardize payment practices, shorten payment terms and promote the healthy development of the automotive industry.

CAAM has been commissioned by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology to conduct the assessment as an independent third-party organization, the industry association said yesterday. The companies under review include leading automakers such as BYD, SAIC, Dongfeng Motor Group, FAW Group and Geely Auto, as well as emerging electric vehicle manufacturers such as Xiaomi Auto, Li Auto, Nio and Xpeng.

The evaluation will be conducted annually and cover several areas, including whether automakers pay suppliers within 60 days, maintain long-term and stable supplier relationships and have built clear and effective accounts payable management systems, CAAM said. It will also examine compliance in aspects such as the proportion of payments made in cash and negotiation mechanisms.

Data will be collected through a combination of regular reporting by carmakers and random checks of selected suppliers, it said. Auto manufacturers must submit reports on their supplier payment practices for the previous calendar year by Jan. 31 each year, followed by reports covering the first half of the current year by July 31.

Over the past few years, intensifying competition in China’s automotive industry has led to increasingly extended supplier payment terms, putting pressure on the healthy development of the broader industry. Against this backdrop, 17 major Chinese carmakers jointly pledged in June last year to keep supplier payment terms within 60 days. CAAM subsequently issued an industry initiative calling on automakers to standardize their payment practices.

In September, the MIIT and the State Administration for Market Regulation rolled out new regulations aimed at standardizing carmakers’ payments to suppliers and improving payment-term management. This effectively elevated what had previously been a voluntary industry self-regulatory initiative into a formal regulatory requirement.

Over the past year, average payment terms among China’s major automakers have shortened significantly, while the proportion of payments in cash has significantly increased, resulting in an overall improvement in payment practices.

However, supplier payments involve multiple stages and practices vary considerably among carmakers. Significant challenges remain in further optimizing payment terms, and Chinese vehicle manufacturers still have room for improvement compared with established multinational automakers, an MIIT official said.

Editors: Dou Shicong, Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese AI Chipmakers Turn to Domestic Suppliers Amid Tighter US Export Controls
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- As the United States further tightens export controls on advanced chips, Chinese artificial intelligence chip manufacturers are strengthening supply chain resilience by partnering with domestic semiconductor suppliers and by developing key technologies in-house.

The new restrictions could disrupt the short-term supply of AI chips in China, industry insiders say. However, the extent of the impact will depend on how strictly the rules are enforced and on whether domestic manufacturers have sufficient capacity.

The interim final rule issued by the US Bureau of Industry and Security on Nov. 16 took effect on Nov. 19. In addition to restricting remote access to advanced computing capabilities, the new rules tighten export control requirements for wafer foundries and outsourced assembly, packaging and testing services. They also introduce global licensing requirements for certain transactions involving advanced chips designed by companies that have not been approved or authorized by the BIS.

In response, Biren Technology said it has already replaced relevant components and services required for product development and manufacturing with domestic alternatives or in-house solutions.

The Shanghai-based company currently sources chip manufacturing and packaging services from domestic suppliers, 21st Century Business Herald reported yesterday.

Iluvatar CoreX’s production and business operations are normal and all business activities are progressing according to plan, the GPU designer said on its WeChat account on Nov. 20. The Shanghai-based firm has established close partnerships with multiple domestic semiconductor supply chain partners to improve supply chain stability and resilience, it added.

AI chipmaker Enflame Technology also said in a statement the same day that it has a healthy order backlog and is working with several domestic semiconductor industry partners to develop cloud-based AI chips using a domestic supply chain. Its production and business operations are proceeding as planned, it added.

Biren, Iluvatar CoreX, Moore Threads Technology and MetaX Integrated Circuits (Shanghai) all operate under a fabless business model, focusing on chip design while relying on external suppliers for wafer fabrication.

Since the announcement, shares of Biren, Iluvatar CoreX, MetaX and Moore Threads have fallen. The first three hit their lowest levels since listing yesterday, but they recovered slightly today.

Long-Term Outlook

"Even the most advanced chip designs must ultimately be turned into physical products through semiconductor manufacturing. Changes to the rules could make it harder for domestic GPU makers to predict production schedules and approval timelines. Even with sufficient orders, firms may need to reassess when and at what scale they can secure manufacturing capacity,” a Technology, Media and Telecommunications industry analyst told Yicai yesterday.

However, the actual impact will depend on how the rules are implemented and how strictly they are enforced, the person added.

“The restrictions may weigh on companies’ financial performance in the short term, but the long-term growth outlook for AI demand has not changed,” the analyst said.

Overseas restrictions could also accelerate the development of China’s advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies, creating opportunities for local wafer foundries, semiconductor equipment makers and materials suppliers, the analyst added.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Huawei, CXMT Challenge South Korean Rivals in Advanced Memory Chip Research
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- China's Huawei Technologies and ChangXin Memory Technologies are pushing into advanced memory chip technologies, stepping up competition with South Korean industry giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix ahead of one of the world's leading chip design conferences.

The four chip developers will showcase their latest research at the 2027 International Solid-State Circuits Conference (ISSCC), held in San Francisco next February. The ISSCC is a major international chip design conference organized by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers Solid-State Circuits Society, a professional body specializing in integrated circuit technology.

The conference agenda shows that Chinese chipmakers are expanding their research into high-bandwidth memory (HBM) architectures, vertical gate transistors, and wafer-level bonding, reflecting a broader shift in global competition toward advanced memory cell design, interface technologies, and chip packaging as artificial intelligence accelerators demand greater memory bandwidth and capacity.

Huawei will unveil its research into a customized HBM architecture at the conference. The Chinese telecoms giant's research paper, titled "A 64-Channel 4096-DQ Custom HBM with Memory Controllers and 5-Layer Wafer-on-Wafer Hybrid Bonding," describes a memory architecture that integrates memory controllers and uses five-layer wafer stacking to support high-bandwidth data transmission.

CXMT, meanwhile, will present research on 32-gigabit double data rate 5 (DDR5) memory featuring vertical surround-gate transistors, designed to improve memory density, and wafer-to-wafer hybrid copper bonding, an advanced technique for directly connecting stacked semiconductor layers. The company will also present separate research on low-power double data rate 6 (LPDDR6) interface technology.

South Korean chipmakers are also pushing the performance limits of HBM. Samsung will present a 48-gigabyte HBM4E memory chip, an enhanced version of HBM4, with a per-pin data transmission rate of 17 gigabits per second.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Tencent’s Hunyuan AI Aims to Develop Bigger Next-Gen Models Without Chasing Benchmarks Leaderboards
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 23 -- Tencent Holdings’ new Hy4 artificial intelligence model still has significant room for improvement, especially in post-training, so the Chinese internet giant’s Hunyuan team said it is investing heavily in large-scale reinforcement learning, aiming to develop a much bigger next-generation model without deliberately chasing benchmark leaderboards during training.

The parameter count of Hy4 and Hy4 flash, released earlier this month, drew particular attention during a two-hour question-and-answer session held by the Hunyuan team, including Tencent’s Chief AI Scientist Yao Shunyu, on Reddit on Nov. 21. While models from ByteDance and Kimi are pushing toward the trillion-parameter mark, Hunyuan remains at around 700 billion.

Compared with models that lean toward coding, the new Hy4 model is more geared toward general-purpose use, the team pointed out. The parameters of the next-generation Hy model are expected to expand significantly, it added.

In addition, one user pointed out that Hy4 inference sometimes takes too long.

Addressing the “overthinking” issue, the Hunyuan team said Hy4’s goal is to maximize intelligence, so overly long chains of thought are a known issue. The team noted it has distilled this capability into the more cost-effective Hy4 flash, which uses reinforcement learning to keep CoT shorter, but acknowledged that “overthinking” is the hardest behavior to fix in post-training.

Creative writing and readability are key focus areas for improvement, with room for progress in these areas, the team pointed out.

Since Yao took charge, Hunyuan abandoned the approach of chasing leaderboards through benchmark scores. Some users noted that Hunyuan has not published results on common benchmarks such as GPQA Diamond and SWE Bench.

These benchmarks were launched early on, so their scores have already saturated, the team said, adding that it instead shows results on newer, more challenging benchmarks such as Agents’ Last Exam. It also stressed that in model development, it addresses certain issues through better training data and diverse internal evaluations, without deliberately pursuing leaderboards.

On whether Hunyuan can catch up with the most cutting-edge models under restrictions on the supply of advanced AI chips, the team said it is squeezing the most out of its existing resources to reach the frontier.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Huawei's Patent Licensing Income Tops USD800 Million in 2025, VP Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- Huawei Technologies earned around USD800 million from patent licensing last year, while the cumulative value of its outbound patent licensing revenue has exceeded USD6.9 billion, according to the vice president of the Chinese technology giant.

Huawei filed its first patent application in China in 1995, and received its first patent licensing revenue in 2011, Alan Fan, who is also chief IP officer of the Shenzhen-based firm, said at the seventh Innovation and IP Forum on Nov. 24. Annual licensing income exceeded outbound licensing payments for the first time in 2021, he pointed out.

As of the end of last year, Huawei had signed more than 260 patent licensing deals with major information and communications technology companies in the United States, Europe, Japan, and South Korea. Some 55 Fortune Global 500 companies have paid it patent licensing fees.

Huawei added 20 new licensees last year across the network and communications equipment, consumer electronics and computing, the Internet of Things, automotive, streaming, semiconductors, and medical devices industries. Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen Group in Europe, Qualcomm, HP, and Harman International Industries in the US, and Seiko Solutions, Mitsubishi Fuso, and Fujitec in Japan are among the companies that have obtained licenses directly from Huawei this year and last.

Huawei licenses its patents through bilateral agreements and patent pools, the latter of which allows companies to obtain licenses from multiple rights holders covered by a licensing program under a single agreement. The firm is the largest contributor to multiple patent pools, including Avanci Video, Sisvel, and Via EVS.

Huawei has also disclosed its licensing programs and royalty rates for standard-essential patents, including those for fifth-generation smartphones, IoT products, and Wi-Fi devices. On June 18, it announced a royalty rate of 50 US cents per unit for consumer-grade Wi-Fi 7 products, unchanged from the corresponding rate for Wi-Fi 6, a decision it says is intended to give the industry predictable licensing costs.

"Global IP institutions set the shared, balanced rules of the road to reward inventors for their investment," said Francis Gurry, former director general of the World IP Organization. "Innovative firms, for their part, turn those rules into real-world practice through voluntary licensing, open collaboration, and responsible technology diffusion."

A neutral, fair, and predictable standard essential patent licensing environment benefits both patent holders and implementers, said Aleš Zalar, director of the Patent Mediation and Arbitration Center of the Unified Patent Court. It protects the value of innovation while reducing barriers to developing and commercializing new technologies, he added.

Patent Portfolio and R&D Investment

More than 3.2 billion 5G devices used Huawei's patented cellular tech as of the end of last year, while over 1.6 billion consumer electronic devices and more than 4.1 billion multimedia devices, excluding mobile phones, used its patented Wi-Fi and video codec tech.

Huawei held more than 165,000 active granted patents worldwide, with over 90 percent being invention patents, according to Emil Zhang, head of its IP strategic planning and key project department. Wireless communications accounted for 41 percent of the portfolio, terminal hardware for 16 percent, and artificial intelligence and computing for 13 percent, he said, adding that the company holds more than 8,000 AI-related patents.

Huawei invested CNY192.3 billion (USD28.9 billion) in research and development last year, accounting for 22 percent of its annual revenue, keeping it above 20 percent for the past five years, with cumulative investment exceeding CNY1.8 trillion (USD270.1 billion) between 2007 and the end of last year.

Huawei's telecommunications research dates back to the 1990s. When China's telephone penetration rate was only about 1 percent in 1992, the company, with just over 100 employees at the time, devoted half of its workforce to developing the C&C08 digital switching system, before gradually expanding from rural to urban markets following its launch.

In 2004, Huawei expanded into the European market with its distributed base stations, an architecture that has since become mainstream in the industry. It began researching 5G technologies in 2009 and subsequently became a major contributor to 5G standards and one of the world's largest holders of such patents.

In 2011, Huawei further integrated its global R&D resources by establishing the 2012 Laboratories to conduct basic research into frontier technologies, including ICT network architectures, standards, and materials, with a five- to 10-year horizon. The labs focus on building medium- and long-term technological capabilities, with some research areas not subject to short-term commercial return requirements, according to the firm.

Eric Xu, Huawei's deputy chairman and rotating chairman, once likened the company's efforts to strengthen basic research to finding its own "Noah's Ark" amid an impending flood of digital information. Its advances in 5G, autonomous driving, Ascend AI computing, and other areas have drawn on research conducted at the 2012 Laboratories.

About one-third of Huawei's annual R&D spending goes toward basic research. The company also operates a non-profit platform for academic exchange, establishing 86 foundational technology labs and more than 180 joint innovation labs and drawing on external expertise by publishing technical challenges and supporting academic research.

Tech Advances

At the Innovation and IP Forum, Huawei presented research advances in LogicFolding, UnifiedBus computing interconnect, near-packaged optics, and other technologies.

The Kirin 9050 Pro project was codenamed "Yellow Crane Tower," with the team drawing inspiration from the traditional Chinese building's multi-level structure, said Liu Yu, a Kirin chipset architect at Huawei. LogicFolding uses a layered circuit design to increase transistor density, Liu pointed out.

The transition from two-dimensional to 3D chip design has also introduced new challenges in design verification, with He Qing, chairman of Phlexing, noting that the chip-design software developer and Huawei have co-developed an electronic design automation tool to verify such multilayer chip designs.

In data center interconnect, Huawei said its UnifiedBus protocol has entered commercial use, making the protocol and compatibility testing specifications available to partners and open-sourcing supporting software.

Huawei's Hi-ONE optical engine, based on near-packaged optics technology, has been commercially deployed, the company said, noting that it is used in its previously unveiled Atlas 960E SuperPoD.

"We look forward to working with partners across every sector to advance technology and industry, and to bring the benefits of innovation to everyone," Fan stressed.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Shein Shares Fall Despite 27% Jump in Third-Quarter Adjusted Net Profit
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- Shares of Shein fell after the Chinese fast-fashion giant reported a 27 percent boost in third-quarter adjusted net profit from a year earlier, as regulatory headwinds continued to weigh on sales in Europe and the United States.

Shein [HK: 0625] closed down 5.8 percent at HKD34.20 (USD4.40) today after the cross-border fast-fashion giant yesterday released its first quarterly earnings report since going public.

Adjusted net profit, which strips out one-off gains and other accounting adjustments to better reflect the profitability of the company’s core business, reached USD790 million in the three months ended Sept. 30, surging more than threefold from the previous quarter, according to the report. Revenue fell 6 percent from a year earlier to USD10.3 billion.

Shein founder Chris Xu expressed optimism about the company's long-term growth prospects despite ongoing challenges in its major markets.

The improvement in adjusted profitability was driven by Shein’s end-to-end business model, which enables the company to maintain control over its operations, quickly adjust its cost structure in response to changing market conditions, and capitalize on emerging business opportunities.

Net profit soared almost eight times to USD4.6 billion in the third quarter, mainly due to a one-off non-cash fair value gain of USD4.1 billion related to convertible redeemable preferred shares.

European Sales Slump, US Outlook Improves

Shein’s sales fell in Europe and the US but grew in other markets.

Shein’s net revenue in Europe plunged 28 percent to USD3 billion in the third quarter from a year earlier. The European Union’s removal of the customs duty exemption for low-value parcels worth up to EUR150 (USD164), coupled with Shein’s price hikes and reduced online advertising spending, led to a decline in sales volumes.

The contraction in European revenue was in line with expectations, Xu said, adding that the market will likely remain under pressure over the next few quarters before gradually recovering in the second half of next year. Shein expects its European revenue to grow more than 10 percent annually over the long term.

Net revenue in the US fell 9 percent to USD2.4 billion, mainly due to an increase in the proportion of orders placed through Shein’s marketplace rather than weakening consumer demand, according to the company. The decline narrowed month by month during the quarter.

Net revenue in other markets jumped 18 percent to USD4.9 billion, driven by growth in orders and the customer base, particularly in Latin America.

The worst is over for Shein in the US market, according to Xu, who expects annual revenue growth to return to the high single digits once market conditions stabilize.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: CGN Starts Building Third Atomic Reactor at Taishan Nuclear Plant in China
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- China General Nuclear Power has broken ground on the third Hualong One reactor unit of the Taishan nuclear power project in Guangdong province, making it the fourth that CGN has started building this year using its flagship third-generation pressurised water reactor.

The first concrete pour for the new Hualong One unit’s nuclear island was completed yesterday, Shenzhen-based CGN announced. It will have the capacity to generate more than 1.2 gigawatts of electricity and produce over nine billion kilowatt-hours a year, enough to meet the annual power needs of about one million people.

This is the second reactor unit the state-owned atomic energy developer has begun building this month, after it completed the first concrete pour of the nuclear island of Unit 4 of the San’ao Nuclear Power Plant in Wenzhou, Zhejiang province, on Nov. 10.

CGN began work on Unit 4 of the Taipingling Nuclear Power Plant in Guangdong in May and Unit 2 of the Zhaoyuan Nuclear Power Plant in Shandong province in September.

The Taishan Nuclear Power Plant, which sits in the southwestern part of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, one of China’s major electricity consumption hubs, will have six atomic power units each with a more than one GW of capacity once all three phases are completed. No final completion date has been announced yet.

The first phase used the third-generation nuclear power technology developed under the leadership of Électricité de France, comprising two units with a unit capacity of 1.75 GW each, which were completed and put into operation in September 2019.

China’s installed nuclear power capacity is expected to lead the world by 2030 and reach 200 GW by 2040, the China Nuclear Energy Association and its related research institutions have predicted.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: Chinese Developer Huafa Properties to Convert USD1.7 Billion Shareholder Loans Into Perpetual Bond
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- Chinese state-backed real estate developer Huafa Properties is planning to convert CNY11 billion (USD1.7 billion) worth of shareholder loans into a perpetual bond, mainly because of its controlling shareholder’s financial struggles.

The perpetual bond, which has no fixed maturity rate, will carry an annual coupon rate equal to the five-year loan prime rate plus 40 basis points, which will not increase if the bond remains outstanding, Huafa Properties announced yesterday. It will have an initial term of three years, after which each term will be extended another three years, with the company having the unilateral option to extend.

Huafa Properties’ controlling shareholder is Huafa Group, a diversified operating platform controlled by the Zhuhai State-Owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission. Its largest source of income is property development, which accounted for more than 38 percent of its total revenue from 2023 to 2025.

Huafa Properties and Huafa Group are both under great pressure from operating performance and short-term liquidity.

Huafa Properties’ revenue fell 34 percent to CNY34.1 billion in the first three quarters of the year from a year earlier, with a net loss of CNY6.4 billion (USD960.7 million). Net cash flow from operating activities was negative CNY302 million (USD45.3 million) in the period, compared with CNY17.4 billion inflow a year ago, indicating a sharp decline in self-financing capacity.

In the third quarter, Huafa Properties' revenue rose 11 percent to CNY15.1 billion from the same period last year. Net loss neared CNY2.8 billion.

Huafa Group had interest-bearing liabilities of more than CNY413 billion (USD62 billion), including CNY181 billion due within a year, as of the end of the first quarter, according to a debt fundraising prospectus. Its net assets were less than CNY185.3 billion, and its asset-liability ratio was close to 76 percent as of March 31.

Converting shareholder loans into a perpetual bond is a financial adjustment made by Huafa Properties with the support of Huafa Group, Song Hongwei, dean of the Tospur Research Institute, told Yicai. “Although it will not bring new cash into the company, it can directly reduce its reported leverage ratio and ease short-term debt repayment pressure.”

In February, Huafa Properties submitted a private placement plan to the Shanghai Stock Exchange, seeking to raise up to CNY3 billion from Huafa Group to fund nine real estate development projects in multiple cities. In July, it reduced the proposed financing amount to CNY2.7 billion and the number of projects to seven.

However, given the difficulties of Huafa Group, the developer said yesterday that it had withdrawn the private placement application.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Futura Costaglione

data.title: China Secures EU's Biggest Hybrid Car Import Quota
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- China has received the largest quota among all import sources subject to the provisional quantitative restrictions on imports of hybrid vehicles that the European Union will impose for 200 days starting Dec. 1. 

China was allocated a quota of about 192,000 vehicles for the 200 days, equivalent to an annual quota of 350,000 units, followed by Japan with about 171,000 units, Türkiye with 126,000 units, and the United Kingdom with 105,000 units. South Korea, Mexico, Morocco, Serbia, and the United States are also subject to country-specific quotas, while Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Ukraine, Kenya, and certain eligible developing countries were exempt.

The provisional safeguard measures will remain in place until June 18 and cover conventional hybrid, mild hybrid, and plug-in hybrid electric vehicles, according to an implementing regulation issued by the European Commission. The quotas will be administered quarterly, with unused allocations carried over to the following three months. Further imports will not be permitted once the applicable quotas are exhausted.

The reference period for calculating the quotas was a key issue in more than 30 rounds of consultations between China and the EU.

Under the standard approach set out in the World Trade Organization's Agreement on Safeguards, China might have received an annual quota of only about 70,000 vehicles if average imports between 2022 and 2024 had been used as the reference, Shi Xiaoli, director of the WTO Research Center at China University of Political Science and Law, told Yicai. Even if last year had been included, the three-year average would have been only about 150,000 units, Shi noted.

The EU imported 302,000 hybrid vehicles from China last year, up from 107,000 units in 2024 and 46,000 units in 2023, according to Eurostat. The country became its largest source of hybrid car imports after overtaking Japan.

China and the EU eventually agreed to use last year's actual imports as the baseline, resulting in an annual quota about 16 percent higher than actual imports. 

China and the EU agreed on three fundamental principles: respect for facts, non-discrimination, and compliance with rules, with the country's quota no lower than that of any other source of EU imports, the Ministry of Commerce said on Oct. 12.

Hybrid vehicles accounted for 46 percent of new car registrations in the EU in the latest reporting period, up from 33 percent in 2023. However, the average profit margin for EU manufacturers of hybrid autos fell 57 percent from 2023 levels, according to European Commission data.

Under the new regulation, hybrid cars originating in China must be accompanied by an export quota certificate issued by the China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Machinery and Electronic Products to qualify for the quota. 

Chinese carmakers are primarily concerned with quota allocation and export procedures at this stage, Chen Huiqing, director of the chamber's legal services department, said to Yicai. Over the longer term, they will optimize their export model portfolios by accounting for profitability, market demand, and brand development, Chen added.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Xiaomi’s Third-Quarter Profit Plunges 68% as Memory Chip Costs Keep Rising
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 26 -- Chinese consumer electronics giant Xiaomi has reported a 68 percent drop in net profit in the third quarter of the year, mainly because of rising costs of key components, such as memory chips, and intensified competition.

Net profit totaled CNY3.9 billion (USD581.5 million) in the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with CNY12.3 billion (USD1.8 billion) a year earlier, the Beijing-based company said in its latest earnings report on Nov. 24. Adjusted net profit shrank 57 percent to CNY4.9 billion, and gross profit margin fell to 20.2 percent from 22.9 percent.

Xiaomi’s revenue fell 5.2 percent to CNY107.2 billion (USD16.1 billion) in the third quarter from a year ago. Revenue from the smartphone business inched down 0.8 percent to CNY45.6 billion, as global shipments plunged 29 percent to 30.7 million units, but the average selling price surged 40 percent to record CNY1,486 (USD223). The business’s gross profit margin improved to 9.2 percent from 8.5 percent.

Memory chip prices are expected to remain elevated through the second quarter of next year, and dynamic random-access memory costs will likely further increase, Xiaomi’s President Lu Weibing said on the earnings call on Nov. 24. There have been no clear signs of weakening demand, and supply is unlikely to increase significantly in the near term, he added.

Revenue from the new energy vehicle, artificial intelligence, and other new initiatives segment declined 18 percent to CNY23.9 billion in the period, with an operating loss of CNY3.4 billion and a gross profit margin of 19.2 percent.

NEV revenue alone plunged 20 percent to CNY22.7 billion, mainly because of lower deliveries and a shift in the product mix, including a smaller proportion of deliveries of the premium Xiaomi SU7 Ultra.

Xiaomi delivered 100,975 vehicles in the third quarter, down 7.2 percent from a year earlier and 3.1 percent from the second quarter, bringing its total deliveries in the first nine months of the year to 286,030 units. On Sept. 7, the firm launched its extended-range electric sports utility vehicle series.

In October, Xiaomi’s overall vehicle deliveries exceeded 50,000 units, a monthly record this year.

Xiaomi signed memoranda of understanding with eight German auto dealergroups at the IFA consumer electronics trade show in Berlin in September. European automotive trade barriers will not change the company’s globalization strategy, Lu said, adding that its cars will enter the German market first in the second half of next year, probably in the third quarter.

Xiaomi’s revenue from the Internet of Things and lifestyle products business reached CNY27.2 billion in the third quarter, while internet services revenue stood at CNY9.5 billion. Its global monthly active users rose 4.1 percent to record 772 million in September.

Research and development expenses increased 2 percent to CNY9.2 billion in the third quarter from a year earlier, with AI-related spending accounting for more than 30 percent of the total in the first three quarters.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Accor Sees Scope for Growth in China as Hotel Demand Shifts Upmarket, Deputy CEO Says
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 25 -- Accor sees ample room to expand its presence in China, though the next phase of growth will look markedly different from the past decade as demand shifts away from economy lodgings toward midscale and premium accommodation, according to the deputy chief executive officer of the French hospitality giant.

The growing need for investment in technology and increasingly complex hotel distribution systems will drive further chain penetration, Jean-Jacques Morin, who is also CEO of Accor's premium, midscale, and economy division, told Yicai and other media outlets on Nov. 19. China accounts for around 20 percent of the Paris-based firm's new hotel openings worldwide, a share that will likely increase, he said.

Accor opened its 800th hotel in China this March. In July, when it had already grown the number to more than 800 across 17 brands in over 50 Chinese cities, it set a goal to exceed 1,600 over the next five to six years.

Future growth in China's hotel industry will differ from that of the past decade, Morin noted. While many budget hotels were built over the last 10 years, demand is shifting toward midscale brands such as Novotel and Mercure, he said.

Last year, the number of rooms at midscale and upscale brand hotels in China increased 15 percent and 11 percent, respectively, outpacing the 9.4 percent growth logged for budget hotels, according to the China Hospitality Association. Mid-range and high-end hotels accounted for about 38 percent of the country's hotel rooms, up from 29 percent in 2019.
 

"So definitely scale matters, because you just don't want to lose ground," Morin said. "You want to satisfy as many people as possible. China is a place where scale still has a long way to go."

China had about 375,000 hotels with 18.74 million rooms as of the end of last year, according to the China Hotel Industry Development Report released by the China Hospitality Association in April. Hotel chain penetration by room count reached 42 percent, up from 40 percent a year earlier, but remained below the more than 70 percent seen in developed countries.

Distribution -- the channels through which hotel operators market and sell their room to customers -- is costly, complex, and constantly changing, Morin pointed out. By joining large hotel chains and paying fees, owners can benefit from investments in distribution and technology that independent hotels would struggle to make, he stressed.

Accor's expansion plans come as its hotel operations in China face pressure, with revenue growth per available room at its premium, midscale, and budget properties remaining negative last quarter, according to its annual earnings report.

Moran also sees potential in China’s relatively untapped market for natural attractions, saying that improved transport accessibility and investment could create opportunities in new tourism destinations.

Accor is also expanding its global investment in lifestyle hospitality. On Nov. 17, the company announced plans to further increase its stake in hospitality company Ennismore for about EUR1.6 billion (USD1.7 billion). London-based Ennismore has nearly 200 hotels and more than 800 restaurants and bars across 40 countries, according to Accor.

Beyond China

For Accor, expanding its hotel network in China extends beyond domestic operations.

"When I do a strategy for China, I do a strategy for the outbound," Morin noted. To attract Chinese travelers to hotels in other markets such as France, Accor first needs to build brand recognition among consumers, he said.

In June, Accor and Chinese hotel operator H World Group announced an expansion of their decade-long alliance to cover direct booking channels and loyalty programs, which have about 430 million members and will continue to operate independently.

Around 100 hotels from either group are available on the other's platform, according to Accor. Morin added that the partnership is still in its early stages. The pair have complementary hotel networks and customer bases in China and overseas. Further integration of their booking channels could create cross-selling opportunities, and local frameworks need to be fully respected, he said.

The tie-up between Accor and H World serves both inbound and outbound travelers. Amid uncertainties in global tourism, Morin emphasized the importance of visa-free entry policies, openness, and stability in attracting international visitors to China.

China is also a market where Accor can learn about technological innovation, with robots becoming relatively common in local hotels, though such services are not widely available elsewhere, Morin said, adding that visiting the country helps management better understand changes in technology and consumer behavior.

In addition, artificial intelligence will not only improve hotel operating efficiency but also change how consumers discover and book hotels, Morin noted. Hotel operators need to ensure their brands and properties are discoverable through large language models and explore ways to facilitate bookings and payments through AI agents, he said.

"You don't decide you want to be the first one, but you certainly don't want to be the last one," he stressed.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: China Unveils First Chipmaking Equipment Quality Standard to Boost Industry Competitiveness
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 25 -- China has set its first quality management standard for semiconductor equipment and components as booming demand for artificial intelligence chips drives growth in the chipmaking machinery industry.

Developed under the leadership of Naura Technology Group, China's largest semiconductor equipment manufacturer, the standard marks a milestone for the industry, which supplies machinery and tools for chipmaking and has long relied on general manufacturing quality standards. It was released yesterday at the 2026 Integrated Circuit Industry Quality Conference and Semiconductor Equipment and Components Industry Standard Promotion Conference.

More than 50 industry experts spent three years developing the standard. Participants included chipmakers Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation and ChangXin Memory Technologies, equipment manufacturers Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment and Piotech, and component suppliers Fortune Precision Equipment, Siasun Robot & Automation, and Inovance Technology.

Building on general quality management standards, the new framework sets requirements across the entire production process, from design and development to procurement, precision manufacturing, delivery, and services, reflecting the semiconductor industry's need for high precision, cleanliness, reliability, product diversity, small-batch production, customization, and full life cycle management.

Improving Quality and Competitiveness

Existing quality standards have limitations when it comes to chipmaking machinery.

Semiconductor equipment production differs from traditional manufacturing, which is characterized by mass production, assembly lines, and standardization, making it difficult to directly apply conventional quality control methods, Naura Chairman Zhao Jinrong told Yicai.

Unified quality management standards can help companies cut costs, reduce waste, improve operational efficiency, and develop industry talent, Wang Yang, Naura's chief quality officer, told Yicai.

Adopting the new standard will help semiconductor equipment and component makers improve quality control and accelerate the development of more advanced products and smarter manufacturing processes, Wang added.

Booming AI demand is driving growth in China's semiconductor equipment industry. Leading domestic equipment makers generally posted revenue growth of 30 percent to 40 percent last year, with visibility into future orders extending 12 to 18 months, according to the global semiconductor industry association SEMI.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s Changan Auto to Sell 10% Stake in EV Brand Avatr for at Least USD479.7 Million
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 13 -- China’s Changan Automobile is seeking to sell a 10 percent stake in its electric vehicle brand Avatr Technology, which is moving ahead with a Hong Kong initial public offering amid shrinking sales and cash reserves, for a minimum of CNY3.2 billion (USD479.7 million).

Changan will list just over 306.5 million Avatr shares for sale on the Shanghai United Assets and Equity Exchange, with the disclosure period running through Dec. 10, the state-owned carmaker announced yesterday. Avatr has a valuation floor of CNY31.8 billion (USD4.8 billion), about in line with its post-money valuation after its Series C funding round in December 2024.

The buyer must pay a CNY500 million (USD75 million) deposit and settle the full purchase price within three working days of signing the equity transfer contract, Changan noted. It must also guarantee that the source of funds is legal and compliant, that the transaction will not hinder Avatr’s IPO, and that it has no competing business with the brand.

The buyer will be expected to provide support mainly in areas such as premium brand sales channel development and overseas market expansion, Changan told Yicai. After the deal closes, the Chongqing-based carmaker will continue backing Avatr in core areas including technology research and development, vehicle manufacturing, and supply chain, it added.

If the entire 10 percent stake is acquired by a single buyer, it would become Avatr’s second-largest shareholder. Changan owns about 41 percent of Avatr, making it the largest shareholder, followed by battery giant Contemporary Amperex Technology with around 9.2 percent. 

Avatr sold 20,160 vehicles from January through May, according to its IPO prospectus. China Passenger Car Association data shows its domestic retail sales dropped below 3,000 last month. Its cash on hand fell to about CNY6.2 billion in late April from CNY9.7 billion on Dec. 31 and CNY19.3 billion at the end of 2024, implying an average monthly burn rate of more than CNY800 million.

For yet-to-be-profitable automakers listed in Hong Kong, sales expectations affect revenue growth and the price-to-sales ratio, while cash reserves and the cash burn rate relate to a company's cash runway, a key metric watched by capital market investors, industry experts told Yicai.

Changan’s shares [SHE: 000625] closed 0.3 percent lower at CNY6.88 (US1.03) each today, while the wider Shenzhen market shed 2.1 percent. The stock has fallen 42 percent so far this year.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Nearly 30 Chinese Robotics Firms Go Under in Last Two Years Despite Rapid Industry Growth
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 25 -- At least 29 Chinese robotics companies have gone bankrupt, been dissolved or ceased operations since 2025, highlighting the challenges of turning technological development into commercially viable businesses despite the industry’s rapid growth, according to Yicai research.

The collapsed firms include several once-promising industry names, such as Dataa Robotics, Smorobot and Wujing Dynamics, according to Yicai’s analysis of data from business information platform ITjuzi and corporate database Qichacha. The latter reportedly ground to a halt just eight months after its establishment.

Most followed the same trajectory. They secured multiple rounds of funding from prominent venture capital firms or major technology companies after their launch and saw their valuations rise steadily. Some even achieved unicorn status, only to fail along the way.

One example is Infore Robotics and Automation, an industrial robotics company founded in March 2020 by Shen Gang, who holds a doctorate in mechanical engineering from the Tokyo Institute of Technology and who serves as the company’s chief executive officer.

The firm was incubated by Infore Group, which belongs to He Jianfeng, the son of Midea founder He Xiangjian. Infore Robotics attracted investment from several institutional investors, including entities affiliated with TikTok operator ByteDance and on-demand services giant Meituan. Its valuation reached USD500 million just 10 months after its founding.

However, the firm's products failed to achieve sales at scale and Infore Robotics entered bankruptcy liquidation proceedings in July this year. The law firm appointed to act as administrator of the liquidation recently told Yicai that the creditors' meeting held in October had yet to reach a conclusion. The company's outstanding liabilities are still being assessed and another meeting will be held later, it added.

Other robotics firms have encountered different challenges. For example, Shanghai-based Dataa Robotics, which positioned itself as the world's first cloud-based robot operator, was unable to establish a viable market and generate sustainable revenue at scale, eventually leading to a cash-flow crisis. While Smorobot managed to sell its swimming pool-cleaning robots, but was weighed down by delays in collecting payments from customers.

Embodied artificial intelligence remains at an early stage of development, said Shen Meng, executive director of Chanson Capital. It will take considerable time for firms to deploy the technology in commercial applications and generate revenue in phases.

Another wave of robotics companies could face closure in the period ahead, said Wang Han, a partner at Laurel Ventures.

For a firm seeking to achieve long-term sustainability, it must be able to translate technology and products into measurable productivity, said a senior executive at a leading robotics company. This means delivering tangible operational value to customers while also taking total operating costs into account.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Bilibili Gains After Reporting Rise in Revenue, Profit and Record DAUs, MAUs in Third Quarter
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 25 -- Bilibili’s shares advanced after the Chinese video streaming site reported increases in both revenue and net profit, as well as record daily and monthly active users, in the third quarter of the year.

Bilibili [HKG: 9626] climbed 10.7 percent to HKD92.35 (USD11.78) in Hong Kong today. Its New York-listed stock [NASDAQ: BILI] rose 1.9 percent to USD11.10 yesterday.

Net profit widened 7 percent to CNY504.1 million (USD75.2 million) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from a year earlier, the Shanghai-based company announced yesterday. Revenue jumped 8 percent to CNY8.3 billion (USD1.2 billion).

Bilibili’s average daily active users increased 5 percent to 123.5 million in the period, with the average daily time users spent on the platform up 14 percent to 121 minutes, exceeding two hours for the first time.

“We drove healthy growth in the third quarter, with record community engagement alongside steady revenue gains and improving profitability," said Rui Chen, chairman and chief executive officer of Bilibili. "DAUs climbed to nearly 124 million, monthly active users increased to 394 million, and average daily time spent rose to 121 minutes, each surpassing its previous peak.”

The advertising business was Bilibili’s main growth engine, with advertising revenue up 20 percent to CNY3.1 billion in the third quarter from a year ago. The top five contributors to the company’s advertising revenue were gaming, online services, digital home appliances, automotive, and e-commerce.

Meanwhile, Bilibili’s gaming business continued to shrink, as related revenue fell 7 percent to CNY1.4 billion, down for the fifth consecutive quarter despite the decline narrowing in the third quarter.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s TuringQ Beefs Up Quantum Computing Supply Chain With New Packaging and Testing Center
data.description:
(Yicai) Nov. 23 -- TuringQ, a Chinese leader in photonic quantum computing, has opened an advanced packaging and testing center in the city of Changsha, marking another step in the company’s efforts to build a complete industrial chain, it said.

As well as research, development, and manufacturing, TuringQ now has advanced packaging and testing capabilities, the Shanghai-based company announced on Nov. 20. The first phase of the new center will be fully operational next year.

Under TuringQ’s plan, the firm aims to gradually build stable capabilities in advanced packaging and testing for photonic chips, as well as the manufacturing of core optoelectronic components.

Advanced packaging and testing is a key link between chip production and end-system applications. It is also vital in the process of using laboratory-scale optical quantum computing technology to create products and achieve industrial-scale deployment, the firm said.

Set up in February 2021, TuringQ makes software and hardware products including photon chips, photon computers, and quantum cloud platforms.

It has raised over CNY1 billion (USD150 million) in its first three years through seven funding rounds, at a valuation of about CNY7 billion. Investors include Legend Capital, SAIC Group, and Oriza Seed.

TuringQ’s application to begin pre-initial public offering tutoring was accepted by the Shanghai branch of the China Securities Regulatory Commission in August, indicating that the company is moving toward listing in the Chinese mainland.

Editor: Tom Litting
